mathematical_model: Per task: registered node ids resolved against test functions (AST); a registration is declared when a lab_task marker on the test (its class, or its pytest.param case) names the task; a task is tied when one of its declared nodes asserts an evidence label (source text); marker declarations naming a task that does not register what they mark are counted; tied tasks whose tied tests never name the task are counted as advisory; JUnit outcomes per node as recorded in the reports.
numerical_result: 168 tasks, 641 task-to-node registrations (401 distinct node ids), 641 declared by a lab_task marker; 0 registrations whose marker does not name the task; 0 marker declarations naming a task that does not register the test; 0 completed/partial tasks without regression tests; 0 dangling node ids; 0 tasks without a tied test; 0 tied tasks whose tied tests never name the task (advisory); JUnit: 639 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped or not run, 2 not recorded (2 of them T168's own nodes, which its own run's record cannot hold).

title: Convert successful experiments into permanent regression tests.
uncertainty: Exact counts; declarations are read from lab_task decorators, label assertions and (advisory) task naming inferred from source text.
unresolved_assumptions: Declarations are read from literal task ids in lab_task decorators of the test or its class, and in the marks of the pytest.param literals of its one parametrize decorator for that case: a module-level pytestmark or a task id computed at run time is not read, and such a registration counts as undeclared.

A label assertion is inferred from source text: mentioning a label is taken as asserting it. Whether a tied test runs its task is not established: a marker declares the tie, and the advisory count only checks that some tied test names the task or its function.
The tolerance-aware comparison with retained reports (ciw lab verify, run by scripts/check_lab.py in CI) is outside this report.
